model.notes: The take rules aim at the judge's recurring mistake: reading heavy retail short crowding after a pump as squeeze risk even when the pump had already stalled. Each take rule pairs that crowding with a momentum cap on the 4h or 1h move, so the cases where the move was still accelerating (which did squeeze the book) stay excluded. The Bybit-only crowding case was left to the existing proposed skip rule for 10x+ shorts with a heavily short Bybit crowd and a 1h move that is not falling.

new.why: A sharp up-hour on a trade burst while open interest falls is shorts covering, not new longs. Once that squeeze has printed, the forced buyers are gone, so a short entered right after has less fuel against it.

Price has already run against the signal on unwinding OI (the squeeze is done) and BTC is not supporting it. This gives a better short price after the adverse excursion has been absorbed, so a moderate 5% stop survives.

Late longs are paying positive funding and chasing with aggressive buys while BTC stalls. This is buying exhaustion: the top of the local push, after which adverse excursion should be small enough for a 3% stop with equal risk.
A rally on thinning activity with a long-heavy crowd is a weak, crowded bounce. The short is entered at the bounce high instead of at the signal.

Longs are crowded and still buying while BTC trends down over 4h. The coin is being held up against market weakness, and the trapped longs make a straight-for path more likely, which fits a short 2% stop.

patterns.notes: Entry rules aim at entering after a squeeze or buying burst has exhausted itself. Exit rules use the states that held in both halves (crowd_bn_top, funding, px_168h, oi_24h) and avoid the already-tested name_floor_share rules. Early closing was negative almost everywhere in close_by_state, so only two narrow close rules are proposed on floor-prone names.
